title: Defining learning objectives: an instructional design problem statement example for Mac users
metaTitle: Defining learning objectives: instructional design problem statement example
description: Learn how to overcome the common instructional design problem of poorly defined learning objectives on your Mac with practical, actionable fixes.
intro: Defining learning objectives is often the most difficult hurdle in the course creation process. If you struggle to draft a clear instructional design problem statement example, your entire project may suffer from misalignment and poor learner outcomes.
tldr: Vague objectives lead to ineffective training and wasted development time.
Focus on observable performance rather than abstract concepts like understanding.
Use Mager's model to define the condition, performance, and criteria for every objective.
Lazur helps you draft and refine your objectives directly on your Mac.

blocks.text: Why defining learning objectives is hard

Many designers approach learning objectives as a box to check rather than a foundation for their work. You might find yourself using words like know, understand, or appreciate. These are not measurable. They do not tell you if the learner can actually perform the required task. This creates a disconnect between what you teach and what the learner needs to do on the job.

You were likely taught that design is a straight line from analysis to evaluation. In reality, it is a messy, iterative process. You work with subject matter experts who have their own ideas. You face pressure to include every piece of information they provide. This leads to bloated courses that lack focus. When your objectives are not clearly defined, you cannot filter out the noise.
Fixes for your instructional design workflow

items: Adopt performance-based objectives: Focus on what the learner does, not what they know.
Use Mager's components: Every objective needs a condition, a performance, and a criterion for success.
Apply constructive alignment: Check that every assessment task directly maps back to a specific objective.
Filter your content: If a slide or video does not help achieve an objective, cut it.

blocks.text: Using your Mac to refine objectives

You have powerful tools at your disposal on macOS. Use Google Docs to draft your initial objectives. Keep a side-by-side view with your project requirements. If you feel stuck, use the dictation features on your Mac to talk through your ideas. Sometimes speaking the objective out loud reveals how vague it really is.

faq.question: Why are my learning objectives failing?
faq.answer: They are likely too abstract. If you cannot measure the objective with an observation or a test, it is not a performance objective.

faq.question: How do I fix vague objectives?
faq.answer: Replace verbs like understand with observable actions like demonstrate, calculate, or write.

costs.title: Wasted development time
costs.text: Building content that does not align with learner needs forces you to redo work.

costs.title: Project scope creep
costs.text: Without clear objectives, it is easy to add unnecessary information that distracts from the goal.

causes.title: Use of non-measurable verbs
causes.text: Words like understand or learn cannot be verified through assessment.

causes.title: Content-first approach
causes.text: Starting with a format like a video or slide deck before defining what the learner should achieve.

fixes.title: Adopt performance-based language
fixes.text: Use action verbs that describe observable behaviors.

fixes.title: Apply Mager's criteria
fixes.text: Include the condition, the performance, and the standard of success in every objective.
